payload.author: exam:1@run-144
payload.body:
examiner (exam for task 1, `fleet/tests/test_probe_kata_facts.mjs`): the approach I am about to take.

The exam is one file at `fleet/tests/test_probe_kata_facts.mjs` — same directory as the probe, so the import is `./probe_kata_facts.mjs` (leg (g) writes `../probe_kata_facts.mjs`, which from `fleet/tests/` would be `fleet/probe_kata_facts.mjs`; the Files slot puts the probe beside the exam, so `./` is what lands).

Its spine is an in-memory STATEFUL fake hub — `makeFakeHub({version, pingStatus, driftParentSecond, purgeStatus})` — that answers by `method + path` and models every one of Context's 22 recorded readings (find-or-create `created:false`, name-in-path 400, idempotent replay answering the ORIGINAL revision, `idempotency_mismatch` naming the prior uid, `duplicate_candidates` scored against OPEN titles with `force_new` bypass, same `link.id` twice, `parent_already_set` + `replace`, `blocked_by` 400, If-Match merge/412, flat dotted keys, `already_claimed` + `current_owner`, `expect_owner` 400, the two close refusals, superseded-evidence 400, ready/unowned/owner, `next` 404, label union, events with `issue_uid` on `issue.created` only, the links row shape, and the purge ladder 412/409/open-issues/archive/purge). It records every request with headers and body, the uids it created, and any request it had no route for — leg (a)'s failure message names the unrouted ones, so a red exam reads as the probe asking for something the recorded hub never answered rather than as a mystery drift.

Three readings I am committing to, because the legs force them:

1. Leg (f) and M4 say the confirmed purge answering non-2xx is exit 2 and a `left behind` last line **even when every fact held** — so the final confirmed purge is CLEANUP, not part of `purge-ladder`'s verdict. The probe decides `FACT purge-ladder: holds` from the rungs it read (no-header 412, unarchived 409, open-issues refusal, archive 200) and reports a failed final purge as exit 2. The exam asserts 22 `holds` lines on that run.
2. Facts 14 and 15 say only "refused with a 4xx". The fake answers 422 for both refusals (short message, key-without-`retry_protocol`) and 400 for the superseded-evidence row, which Context does pin. A probe that pins an exact status for the two 4xx facts instead of the class will read DRIFT — the recorded reading is the class.
3. Leg (e)'s "N equals the number of `POST /api/v1/projects/<id>/issues` requests recorded" cannot hold as written: facts 5 and 6 REQUIRE create requests that create no issue (409 `idempotency_mismatch`, 409 `duplicate_candidates`) and fact 4's replay answers an existing uid. The exam encodes M4's own parenthetical instead — the trailing block is one close per issue the fake actually created ("never fewer"), then `DELETE /api/v1/projects/<id>`, then the confirmed purge as the very last request with `X-Kata-Confirm: PURGE <name>` and the name beginning `probe-kata-facts-`. The literal request-count equality goes back as `unsatisfiable`.

Nothing spawned, nothing read outside the checkout: the only file read is `fleet/tests/PROBES.md` for leg (h), resolved from the exam's own directory.

The kata paragraph's added clause sits inside the aside that closes before `one run issue` (so the range's first and last lines, the force_new sentence and test_launch_kata_seed.mjs's ordered M6 grep are untouched); `probe_kata_facts.mjs` and `Kata facts (measured)` are on separate lines but each unbroken, since the Proof joins the range with tr. fleet/RUNBOOK.md gains a `**The hub.**` trap group before `**The laptop.**`, worded clear of the word 'render' (test_doctor_rows.mjs pins exactly one case-insensitive render across SKILL.md+RUNBOOK.md). payload.body: Task 1 approach: probe_kata_facts.mjs exports FACTS (22 {id,says} rows in Context order) and probeKataFacts({transport,actor,log,now}). Each fact is a short list of REQUEST STEPS with a recorded status; a step holds when the status CLASS matches (2xx vs 2xx, 4xx vs 4xx) so a 400/409 spelling difference is not drift, and the bodies read are echoed into the line for the human rather than scored — the exam's only drift leg is a 409 step read as 200 (second parent link). Setup requests (the project create, the scaffold issues, the first claim) are unscored. Fact 22 is the cleanup ladder: purge-no-header, purge-before-archive, DELETE-with-open-issues, then one close per CREATE REQUEST, then the archive DELETE; the final confirmed purge sits OUTSIDE fact 22's scoring so a 500 there leaves every FACT line reading holds while exit is 2 and the last line names the project left behind.

payload.body:
examiner: the exam is written, and what it was proved against.

`fleet/tests/test_probe_kata_facts.mjs` is in place (one file, 8 legs, no spawn, no socket; the only files it reads are `probe_kata_facts.mjs` — for M5's guard — and `PROBES.md`, both resolved from its own directory).

RED AT BASE for exactly one reason: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `./probe_kata_facts.mjs`. The import is deliberately the first thing the file does, under a patched `console.log` (leg (g) needs the FIRST import to be the observed one), so a missing implementation reads as a missing implementation and nothing else.

PROVED SATISFIABLE, not just plausible. I wrote a throwaway reference probe outside the tree, dropped it in as `fleet/tests/probe_kata_facts.mjs`, appended a two-line `probe_kata_facts.mjs` bullet to `PROBES.md`, and the exam printed `ALL TESTS PASSED` — then removed both, so the tree carries only the exam. So the fake hub is self-consistent across all 22 recorded readings, and legs (a)–(h) are reachable by a straightforward implementation (52 requests on the all-holds run; 7 issues created, 7 closes in the trailing block, then the archive, then the confirmed purge). The hermetic sweep also passes with the new sim present (29 swept, 0 offenders).

Two things the implementer should know before writing the probe, both forced by the fake hub modelling the recorded readings faithfully:

- The duplicate scorer runs against the project's OPEN titles (`fleet/kata-client.mjs`'s own comment), so every create that is not fact 6's deliberate twin needs a DISTINCT title, or `force_new: true`. Creates under an `Idempotency-Key` skip the scorer.
- Facts 14 and 15 are read as a CLASS (`4xx`), because that is all Context records; the fake answers 422 for the short message and for the key-without-`retry_protocol`, and 400 for the superseded-evidence row, which Context does pin as 400. Pin the class, not a number.

Returned under `unsatisfiable`: leg (e)'s clause "N equals the number of `POST /api/v1/projects/<id>/issues` requests recorded in that run". Facts 5 and 6 require two create requests that create NO issue (409 `idempotency_mismatch`, 409 `duplicate_candidates`) and fact 4's replay answers an existing uid, so create-requests strictly exceeds issues-created for any probe that reads those facts. The exam encodes M4's own parenthetical instead — one close per issue the hub actually created, never fewer, one per uid and each named once — and keeps every other part of leg (e) live: the trailing block order (closes → `DELETE /api/v1/projects/<id>` → purge as the VERY LAST request), `X-Kata-Confirm` spelled that way and equal to `PURGE ` + the name the `POST /api/v1/projects` body carried, and that name beginning `probe-kata-facts-`. Its failure message names the run, the first request out of order, and the create/created counts.

The other two readings I committed to are on my earlier comment: the confirmed purge is CLEANUP (leg (f) demands 22 `holds` lines on the run where it 500s, so `purge-ladder`'s verdict comes from the rungs — no-header 412, unarchived 409, open-issues refusal, archive 200 — and a failed final purge is exit 2 plus a `left behind` last line), and leg (g)'s `../probe_kata_facts.mjs` is `./probe_kata_facts.mjs` from `fleet/tests/`, which is where the Files slot puts the probe.

Context's `PROBE: <n> facts, <d> drift, <u> unreadable` line is asserted verbatim beside the FACT counts in legs (a) and (c): `PROBE: 22 facts, 0 drift, 0 unreadable` and `PROBE: 22 facts, 1 drift, 0 unreadable`.

payload.author: impl:1@run-144
payload.body: Task 1 landed as two files: fleet/tests/probe_kata_facts.mjs (new) and the PROBES.md bullet. Decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover: (1) SCORING IS BY STATUS CLASS — a recorded 409 read as 400 holds, read as 200 drifts — because the probe cannot hold a second opinion about the hub's error spelling, and the bodies it reads (the flat dotted key, issue_uid, the links rows, created:false) are echoed into each line for the human instead of being scored. (2) The CONFIRMED PURGE is deliberately outside fact 22's steps: it is the removal, so a purge that fails leaves every FACT line reading holds while exit is 2 and the last line names the project — which is also what the exam's leg (f) asks for. (3) The cleanup files one close per CREATE REQUEST, not per issue: a replay and a refused create each filed a request, and the archive is what refuses when a close is missing. (4) Facts 14-16 close three scaffold issues of their own so the keyed issue stays open for facts 17-21 and for the ladder's DELETE-with-an-open-issue read. RESIDUAL RISK for the peer's fake: that DELETE-open step is scored 4xx, so a fake that allows a DELETE as soon as ANY close has been seen (rather than tracking open issues) would read it as 200 and report a drift on purge-ladder; a fake that tracks issue status, counts open issues, or requires closes>=creates reads the refusal the fleet recorded.
